creator: shughes@mozilla.com
description:
Currently, for the split Spotlight layout, the main section (with content) is on the right and the secondary section (with illustration) is on the left. For the "Launch Import - Embedded Modal - all users" experiment [we'd like to reverse them](https://www.figma.com/file/0uccbIjwH69dwzsE6L9sEw/Embedded-import-data-spotlight?type=design&node-id=113-17584&mode=design&t=zAUWehD5lmF3mRwT-4), because our illustrations will be quite elaborate, with embedded text and mockups of the browser UI. If those illustrations are on the left, users may be distracted from the interactive content. So we'd like the interactive content to be on the left and the illustrations to be on the right.

Preliminary investigations have shown this is pretty straightforward, but it will need to be QAed to make sure there aren't any unanticipated issues.

Additionally, this would be a good place to test this new kind of illustration that takes up the entire space of the secondary section. Past illustrations have been smaller than the secondary section's illustration box. We should check that the secondary section can accommodate an illustration that is the full size of its dimensions, without any issues with the illustration's edges aligning exactly with the container div's edges. If there are issues, they should be fixed in this bug.
summary: Add the ability to reverse left/right sections of split Spotlight layout

creator: shughes@mozilla.com
description:
For the "Import- Embedded Modal - all users" experiment, we're using illustrations that take up the entire space of the illustration area. But when the window is too small to accommodate the full split Spotlight card, it shrinks to a half-width card, where the secondary section is displayed above the main section, as a tiny banner. The illustration is rendered in this banner area using a "fill" tiling approach rather than a "fit" approach, so most of these giant illustrations will be cut off, making them useless.

In the future, we may add the ability to provide 2 different illustrations: one for normal mode, and one for RDM. But right now, doubling the number of illustrations needed for this experiment is too much. So instead we will be okay with simply disabling RDM for these messages. So that means adding a property that will translate to an HTMl attribute that can be referenced in the RDM styles.

Investigate what happens when RDM is disabled. Does that change the window's minimum width? What if you set a `min-width` rule on the outer container of the `.spotlightBox` (i.e. the container of the browser the document is rendered in, styled in [browser.css](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/b9d9a1a873302452fc918505d62cd226d81b67d0/browser/base/content/browser.css#1441))? Otherwise, do scrollbars appear? This is really an open-ended assignment, since we don't have any preconceptions about how this should be handled. Try to produce the best result for cases where the window is sized really small, but don't sweat it too much, as there is no optimal solution — that's what RDM is ultimately for. In this case, we're making an informed tradeoff on the basis that most users' windows will be much bigger than this.

Note: we also considered adding a targeting attribute for "current window size." The problem is that window size can be changed after the message shows, so it doesn't really solve our problem — we'd still have to disable RDM for these messages. And if we're disabling RDM and it's still possible for the spotlight to render in too small a window, then it seems superfluous to exclude users with already-tiny windows.
summary: Add the ability to disable split Spotlight RDM

creator: shughes@mozilla.com
description:
[The current Figma spec](https://www.figma.com/file/0uccbIjwH69dwzsE6L9sEw/Embedded-import-data-spotlight?type=design&node-id=115-19074&mode=design&t=zAUWehD5lmF3mRwT-4) for the "Import- Embedded Modal - all users" experiment envisions some changes to the embedded migration wizard.

- Most notably, it should be possible to disable the wizard's internal title, so an alternative title and subtitle (provided by the message JSON and rendered in the standard title and subtitle elements) can be shown above it.
- For the collapsed variant, it should be possible to change the expander text from "Import all available data" to "Options", and to hide the expander subtitle (which lists all the available data types), to reduce the initial screen footprint of the wizard and make it less visually overwhelming.
- Make the "Everything" checkbox optional, since we need to remove it to make everything fit nicely.
- Also consider reducing (or making configurable) the block margins between the checkbox items in the initial wizard screen.
- Work on any other discrepancies you notice between the embedded wizard as implemented and the wizard as it appears in the latest designs.
summary: Update the embedded migration wizard to support configurations from Figma

creator: mcheang@mozilla.com
description:
In Bug 1852527, I added telemetry for when the default engine's property is updated. (engine-update). 
We discovered that our telemetry is not very specific when it comes to reloading engines due to a config change. 

At the moment, when we reload due to a configuration change, we update the engines as they may have changed: [engine.updateIfNoNameChange](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/734887cfb193b5697e59a857d394e8d4245996db/toolkit/components/search/SearchService.sys.mjs#1945-1948). However, we don't track if any attribute has actually changed from previous, and so we send out an update regardless: [#updateFromManifest](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/734887cfb193b5697e59a857d394e8d4245996db/toolkit/components/search/AddonSearchEngine.sys.mjs#366,370)

We should consider adding more specificity on when we report the telemetry, some options:

1) Only notify when something on the search engine has actually changed
2) when reloading engines, have a special observer notification to indicate that all engines may have changed.

This bug may be a good spike to do during a DragonSlayer - spend a few hours experimenting and seeing what we'd like it to look like, and implement it.
summary: Add more specificity on when to record telemetry on reloaded due to a config change (search engine changed, engine-update)

description: We only check for `GetAllowPlugins` (indirectly) in [`nsWebBrowserContentPolicy::ShouldProcess`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/toolkit/components/browser/nsWebBrowserContentPolicy.cpp#60). However that code is dead, because in [`nsObjectLoadingContent::CheckProcessPolicy`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/961556b584938a694d7df6e7bf25d70253c37060/dom/base/nsObjectLoadingContent.cpp#651) `objectType` can only be `TYPE_DOCUMENT` (and not `TYPE_OBJECT` as expected by `WebBrowserContentPolicy`). creator: kwright@mozilla.com
description:
This bug was created in response to issues with QoS priority found in bug 1864641. It's possible that a mainthread finds itself unable to wake up during shutdown, due to being put into the background during the shutdown process. The entire content process then gets stuck, because the main thread is idle.

I can't prove that this is the issue we're seeing in the above bug, but plugging this hole in the code will ensure that we don't run into this issue in the wild (if we are). A simple solution is to just signal before we send the first shutdown signal that we want to warm up the main thread, and ignore all QoS change calls after that. We're completely fine to ignore QoS change calls if the most recent change set the main thread to its highest priority.
summary: Prevent main thread QoS priority changes during shutdown

creator: michaelahughesuk@gmail.com
description:
For the Chromium dual browser extension to work (to launch a site in Firefox), there needs to be a mechanism to determine if Firefox is installed and registered as a handler for the firefox: and firefox-private: protocols. The Dual Browser extension will attempt to connect to a native messaging client, which will return an error if the native messaging client is not registered, indicating Firefox isn't installed.

So, Firefox needs to register itself as the native message handler of this type, in the same places in the code that it registers itself as the handler for the above protocols.

https://developer.chrome.com/docs/apps/nativeMessaging/#native-messaging-host-location
summary: Modify Firefox to register itself as a native messaging client for Chrome for the Dual Browser extensions on Windows

creator: dmosedale@mozilla.com
description:
Meeting with security folks as part of the [Rapid Risk Analysis](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1874503), we agreed on a two-pronged security architecture for getting click-through rate data to the Skylight web-app:


-[ ] Request a service account on BigQuery for Skylight
-[ ] Spike the queries we're going to want for the CTRs (message CTR - time period?) and CTR change (time period?), with and without experiment restrictions
-[ ] Work with the SRE team to restrict access to that service account to just reading the columns of the tables we need.
-[ ] Set up the Netlify Auth0 plugin so Skylight requires LDAP authentication.  Work with the IAM team as needed.

Part of this will be to spike the BigQuery query we need to get the CTR numbers and arrow direction for this [design](https://www.figma.com/file/pFX5NRHYTegMHzqNKk3KdH/Messaging-system?type=design&node-id=843-5711&mode=design&t=TTwvDnLLDMIRErPz-4) and prototype that in the app.
summary: spike making Skylight CTR data into the web app

creator: mstange.moz@gmail.com
description:
This bug is implementing a change which is not visible to Firefox users and only matters to developers using external profilers with custom builds of Firefox locally.

---

For profiling Firefox with external profilers, we currently use two supplemental files to write down profiling-related information:

 - JIT function information goes into a jitdump file, which can be consumed by samply on macOS and Linux. On Windows we use separate ETW JIT events instead.
 - Marker information goes into a marker file (enabled by `MOZ_USE_PERFORMANCE_MARKER_FILE`). This is consumed by etw-gecko and by a development version of samply (with custom patches on various samply branches).

To associate the information in those files with what's happening in the profile, we need to put timestamps into the files.

At the moment we use these timestamps, depending on the platform:

 - On Linux and Android, we use `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` nanoseconds for both.
 - On Windows, we don't use jitdump, and the marker file uses `TimeStamp::RawQueryPerformanceCounterValue()`.
 - On macOS, we use `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` nanoseconds for jitdump and `TimeStamp::RawMachAbsoluteTimeValue()` for the marker file.

The inconsistency on macOS is not good and I would like to fix it in this bug.

On macOS, I want both jitdump and the marker file to use "nanoseconds since mach_absolute_time origin". This value has the advantage that it is also relatively easy to obtain in other browser engines.
summary: Change jitdump timestamps on macOS to be relative to the mach_absolute_time origin, and change MOZ_USE_PERFORMANCE_MARKER_FILE timestamps to match

creator: jsnajdr@gmail.com
description:
Steps to reproduce:
1. Be logged in into a site like `wordpress.com` as first party, have first party cookies stored for the site.
2. Go to a different site like `example.blog` which embeds an iframe from `wordpress.com/embed`.
3. This iframe is loaded without cookies, because 3rd party cookies are blocked. That's expected.
4. In the `wordpress.com/embed` iframe, request storage access with `document.requestStorageAccess()`. It's granted.
5. Now, create a _nested_ iframe in the `wordpress.com/embed` iframe, and load a same-origin document into it, like `wordpress.com/helper`.

What I expected:
The `wordpress.com/helper` iframe is loaded with the first-party cookies for `wordpress.com`, because access to them has been explicitly granted.

What actually happened:
There are no cookies on the `wordpress.com/helper` request. On the other hand, if I do exactly the same request using `fetch('./helper')`, the first-party cookies are there. It's only the iframe request that omits them.

Chrome, in the same situation, would always send the `wordpress.com` cookies. Both on same-origin nested iframe (`wordpress.com/*`) and also on same-site nested iframe (`public-api.wordpress.com/*`).

I'm using the latest Firefox Nightly 124.0a1 (2024-01-24) (64-bit)
summary: With storage access granted, nested iframe is loaded without cookies

creator: maltejur@dismail.de
description:
Created attachment 9376430
Screenshot_20240125_130700.png

When entering a URL without a scheme in the address bar, the first result suggests that it will be fixed up with a http:// scheme (see screenshot). With the introduction of schemeless HTTPS-First in Bug 1812192, that not the case anymore, as we will try a https scheme first, and then fall back to http if https isn't available. I am wondering what the best fix for this is. I think we should either:

1. Change the scheme displayed to https://. This would make sense, as most inputs will indeed end up as https:// URIs. But crucially, this is not the case all the time. So I am not sure if it is a risk to display the user that the site will load via a secure connection, when it is still possible that we fall back to http.
2. Just do not display the http:// scheme anymore when there is a schemeless input. This would kind of align with Bug 1850491. If we would go this route, we will also have to think about if we want to display the scheme for inputs that do have a https:// scheme. For consistency with the address bar and schemeless inputs, I think we should also drop the scheme in that case.
summary: Address bar should not prefix schemeless URI that will be handled by schemeless HTTPS-First

description: There are two places in `nsSSLIOLayerSetOptions` where we are comparing `infoObject->GetProviderFlags()` against `nsISocketTransport` flags instead of `nsISocketProvider` flags. Since xyber768d00 is pref'd off by default, we don't need to fix this on the Fx123 branch.

Currently when we use the logging functions of `ConsoleInstance`, we obtain the preference value (if there is an associated pref), then look it up in the enumerated list of `ConsoleLogLevelValues` and finally convert it to a log level integer.

We can improve this by caching the computed log level value, and adding a preference listener.

creator: dholbert@mozilla.com
description:
I noticed when reviewing bug 728807 that the pref `layout.scrollbar.side` is currently defined in `all.js` here:
https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/cee2c396081d950f9e3401113fb179999e404ab8/modules/libpref/init/all.js#1964-1969

...but that's sort of out-of-place and perhaps suboptimal-when-we-read-it, since we have to go through `Preferences::GetInt()` which I think is a little slower than `StaticPrefs`:
https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/cee2c396081d950f9e3401113fb179999e404ab8/layout/base/nsPresContext.cpp#441

It fits the [criterion for StaticPrefList.yaml](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/cee2c396081d950f9e3401113fb179999e404ab8/modules/libpref/init/StaticPrefList.yaml#5-6) which is "static prefs, i.e. those that are defined at startup and used entirely or mostly from C++ and/or Rust code". Let's move it there.
summary: Move layout.scrollbar.side to StaticPrefList.yaml

David Bokan <bokan@chromium.org> wrote:
>  vt: Snapshot containing block resize skips transition
>  
>  This CL adds a check for the snapshot containing block (SCB) changing
>  before capturing new state. We already checked for a changed SCB on each
>  animation frame, however, this check corresponds to the check that
>  occurs in the Activate View Transition[1] steps of the spec. This
>  difference is web-observable since, without this line, the transition
>  isn't skipped until animation frames are being produced. This means we
>  don't reject the `ready` promise, as a strict reading of the spec would
>  imply.
>  
>  This was also an issue in same-document view transitions (i.e. triggered
>  by `startViewTransition()`). This CL affects both same- and
>  cross-document transitions.
>  
>  [1] https://www.w3.org/TR/css-view-transitions-1/#activate-view-transition:~:text=transitions%20to%20false.-,If%20transition%E2%80%99s%20initial%20snapshot%20containing%20block%20size%20is%20not%20equal%20to%20the%20snapshot%20containing%20block%20size%2C%20then%20skip%20the%20view%20transition%20for%20transition%2C%20and%20return.,-Capture%20the%20new

>  Add WebSocketError for WebSocketStream
>  
>  WebSocketError is a subclass of DOMException that has `closeCode` and

>  A WebSocketError object can be passed to the writer abort() and reader

**Expected behavior:** The copied link should be [https://youtu.be/mXKWlJ5ugg4?t=588](https://youtu.be/mXKWlJ5ugg4?t=588) or [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mXKWlJ5ugg4?t=588](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mXKWlJ5ugg4?t=588), the latter even forgoing the `&feature=youtu.be` tracking parameter that would get re-added when following the former link.

creator: botond@mozilla.com
description:
In a few places (especially in the implementation of other `Matrix4x4Typed` functions), we have to cast a matrix from one set of source and target units to another ([example](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/cee2c396081d950f9e3401113fb179999e404ab8/gfx/2d/Matrix.h#1321-1328)).

We currently do this by using `ToUnknownMatrix()` and `FromUnknownMatrix()` to round-trip the type through `UnknownUnits`, which adds an unnecessary copy. This unnecessary copy could be avoided by adding a `Cast<NewSourceUnits, NewTargetUnits>()` function that does the type change in a single call.
summary: Add a Matrix4x4Typed::Cast function

creator: rpigott@berkeley.edu
description:
User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64; rv:122.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/122.0

Steps to reproduce:

The WaylandIdleInhibit WakeLockType is regressed by [1].

The wakelock is disabled anytime it fails to acquire the lock in [2], but the InhibitWaylandIdle() method may return false for benign reasons, like firefox not having focus [3]. Firefox should use another surface in this case, ideally whichever one has the playing video.

Once the WakeLockType is disabled it won't be re-enabled, meaning if a video begins playing while firefox is not focused, idle inhibit will remain broken for the remainder of the session, even in cases where it otherwise would have succeeded.

[1] https://hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/rev/1c8dec8815d59d488dc44109a4361dcec573ec0a
[2] https://hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/rev/1c8dec8815d59d488dc44109a4361dcec573ec0a
[3] https://hg.mozilla.org/mozilla-central/rev/1c8dec8815d59d488dc44109a4361dcec573ec0a#l1.573


Actual results:

Firefox does not inhibit idle in a wayland session while playing video, if playback begins while the browser is not focused.


Expected results:

Firefox should always acquire the idle inhibitor, regardless of focus, and ideally should not permanently disable idle inhibition if it fails to acquire the inhibitor for whatever reason. It is compositor policy when to enforce the inhibition, so the client does not and should not have a need to know if the surface is focused or visible.
summary: [Wayland] wayland idle inhibit broken

creator: jdemooij@mozilla.com
description:
Adding a new pref for a new feature or optimization currently requires *a lot* of boilerplate code. This is error-prone and we're spending quite a lot of time just adding/changing/removing/reviewing prefs.

I'm working on patches that eliminate almost all of this boilerplate by parsing `StaticPrefList.yaml` at SpiderMonkey build time and generating code to automatically read the `javascript.options.*` prefs.

To add a pref using this new system, all that is needed is:
1. Add the pref to `StaticPrefList.yaml`, for example `javascript.options.amazing_new_feature`.
2. Use `JS::Prefs::amazing_new_feature()` to retrieve its value in JS engine code.

Both JS shell and browser builds will default to the default value in `StaticPrefList.yaml`. In the JS shell, it'll be possible to set a pref value with `--setpref amazing_new_feature=true` or a custom shell flag or whatever.

At least initially this will only support process-wide prefs that are set at startup, but for 95% of our prefs that's all we need.
summary: Make StaticPrefList.yaml prefs available in SpiderMonkey

creator: botond@mozilla.com
description:
In our APZ gtests, we have a utility method named [`APZCTesterBase::Tap()`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/c88ac92342d525fd69dbd4c29cd22984eaf9de78/gfx/layers/apz/test/gtest/APZTestCommon.h#619).

This method has an optional output parameter named `aOutInputBlockId`, which can be used to communicate the id of the input block created by the tap back to the caller.

Since bug 1678505, this function also returns an `APZEventResult`, which contains the same input block id in the field `mInputBlockId`.

This makes the output parameter redundant (checking the field of the return value is a better way for the caller to get the input block id). We should remove it, and transition any callers that use it to use the return value instead.
summary: Remove the aOutInputBlockId parameter of APZCTesterBase::Tap()

>  [wpt] Fix unhandled rejection in `scrollend-event-not-fired-...html`
>  
>  This WPT checks for the absence of a scrollend event by waiting for the
>  `waitForScrollendEvent()` helper to reject. However, if the rejection
>  occurs before attaching handlers, the rejection may be returned when
>  running the test with WebDriver [1] and cause the overall harness status
>  to flake. The `promise_test()` can still pass because it only awaits the
>  handled promise.
>  
>  De-flake the test by immediately attaching the handlers. See also: [2].

I'm stubbing out the existing triage rotation from the doc into the tree right now, but it's going to run out in April. Also, as the year goes on inevitably there are new people (yay!) and people moving to other teams or leaving (sadfaces). So we'll need to update the schedule. 1. get a list of everyone who should be in this rota

3. distribute people across the calendar from those groups, trying to mix teams / seniority levels
4. update gdoc per (3)

creator: adw@mozilla.com
description:
A few days ago the order of the `RemoteSettingsConfig()` params [was changed](https://github.com/mozilla/application-services/commit/b324e64a3d80521a824793fcce04252f881a83df). Once that revision is vendored into m-c, we'll need to update [SuggestBackendRust](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/2a867dd1ab015c3ef24b774a57709fb3b3dc4961/browser/components/urlbar/private/SuggestBackendRust.sys.mjs#173-177). In the meantime, if you're testing a vendoring locally, you'll need to update the backend because otherwise you'll get an unhelpful generic "Error initializing SuggestStore" error.

The new ordering is: collection, bucket, server -- as below:

```js
          new lazy.RemoteSettingsConfig(
            "quicksuggest",
            lazy.Utils.actualBucketName("main"),
            lazy.Utils.SERVER_URL
          )
```
summary: Update RemoteSettingsConfig call for new parameter order

description:

See https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D199763#6860039 for more context.

creator: lougenia@mozilla.com
description:
Created attachment 9377267
Screenshot 2024-01-30 at 4.23.28 PM.png

Beginning on 1/23/24 the sync success rates for the clients and tabs engines on Firefox Desktop beta began to decline (see [here](https://sql.telemetry.mozilla.org/queries/85526?p_Days=60&p_channel=beta&p_engine_name=all-engines#211801) for details). There was also a drop in the clients engine sync success rate on Nightly starting 1/13/24 which _*may*_ be related (see [here](https://sql.telemetry.mozilla.org/queries/85526?p_Days=60&p_channel=nightly&p_engine_name=all-engines#211801)). The tabs engine success rate on Nightly is also decreasing, but much more gradually.

Checking the [Desktop Sync Error Message graph](https://sql.telemetry.mozilla.org/queries/86456?p_channel=beta&p_engine_name=all-engines#214076) there is an increase in remote setup failure and UTF-8 errors for both the tabs and clients engines around the same time period.
summary: Decline in sync success rates for tabs and clients engines on Beta

Dan Clark <daniec@microsoft.com> wrote:
>  [EditContext] Ensure textupdate fires for backspace/delete in <canvas>
>  
>  When the active EditContext's associated element is a \<canvas>, we
>  fail to fire the textudpate event when the user hits backspace/delete.
>  
>  The reason is that for these keystrokes, EnabledInEditableText is
>  used to determine whether the command is enabled, and this includes
>  a check that the selection is contained in the focus. For \<canvas>
>  this will never be the case because \<canvas> cannot contain selection.
>  
>  Fix this by always treating the command as enabled if there is an
>  active EditContext, since an EditContext should always have the
>  opportunity to handle these commands.
>  
>  Update some existing text input and text deletion tests to run for
>  \<canvas> in addition to \<div>.

description:
Bug 1770944 needs to remove  `mInIsolatedMozBrowser` member from `OriginAttributes` but storage upgrade functions still need to use it. We already had to add custom parsing when `mAppId` was removed: https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/2a867dd1ab015c3ef24b774a57709fb3b3dc4961/dom/quota/ActorsParent.cpp#7614

I think it's now time to add a special class which can handle all origin attributes for storage upgrade purposes.
summary: Introduce StorageOriginAttributes class

creator: dholbert@mozilla.com
description:
STR:
1. Load https://twitter.com/i/status/1489727779411214339
(No need to sign in. Dismiss any popups about notifications/etc. that get in the way.)

2. Click the play button in the center of the video (or the video might just attempt to start playing on its own)


ACTUAL RESULTS:
The video never loads/plays. There's just a spinning throbber overlay that spins forever.

EXPECTED RESULTS:
Video should load/play.

Chrome gives EXPECTED RESULTS.
Firefox 124.0a1 (2024-01-30) (64-bit) gives ACTUAL RESULTS.
So does Nightly 111.0a1 2023-02-01 and a few other nightlies in between that I tested -- so, this seems to not be a regression or a recent one.
(I also tried spoofing a Chrome UA string, but that didn't make a difference.)


Note, this is similar to old/fixed bug 1764293, but the embedded video from that bug does play correctly in Firefox for me.  So there's something special about the video that I've linked here that makes it specially-broken.
summary: Twitter/X video fails to play in Firefox

creator: bugmail@asutherland.org
description:
In a [slack thread](https://mozilla.slack.com/archives/C495VS94P/p1706203492200009) there were reports of a problem with the "Labels" sidebar mechanism in Google Docs which after brief investigation appeared to correlate with ServiceWorkers and in particular `NS_ERROR_INTERCEPTION_FAILED` errors on subresource fetches (which we don't have any current mitigations for).  After additional investigation over Zoom and local reproduction, it appears that the problem occurs only on Release (Firefox 122) but not Nightly (Firefox 124).

Complicating matters, if devtools is connected to the ServiceWorker when the fault occurs, devtools disconnects for some reason and this [induces the ServiceWorker to terminate](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/2c3d657cbba5484ccac44443c4417baed7b5fafb/dom/serviceworkers/ServiceWorkerPrivate.cpp#1260-1266).

Using the Profiler we can see an "unhandledrejection" event firing, but cannot see its content.  Interestingly, an "updatefound" event is also being fired.

I plan to continue my investigation tomorrow with the primary goal of identifying the unhandledrejection and why nightly doesn't care.
summary: ServiceWorker failure for drive.google.com which breaks Google Drive/Docs Labeling sidebar

creator: gpascutto@mozilla.com
description:
In bug 1872920 an (alleged) security issue got reported and after talking  to reporter it turned out he was using a (unknown, but presumably a VM) configuration where remote WebGL get disabled, causing us to disable win32k lockdown: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1872920#c8

I can confirm this behavior on an Mac M1, using Parallels: https://paste.rs/ZPeq6.txt

We specifically intended for this not to happen, see e.g.: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1736605#c6

Code inspection also doesn't reveal why we end up disabling remote WebGL or in what conditions that would happen.

@ahale investigated and found: *"When I try to repro, Windows 11 23H2 running in VMware Workstation on Windows 11 23H2, I see IsWebglIsOutOfProcessEnabled: 1 in the Graphics - WebGL 1 Driver WSI Info section and Win32k Lockdown State for Content Process - Win32k Lockdown enabled -- default value is true"*
summary: Missing Remote WebGL causing Win32k Lockdown Disable on some VM

creator: shughes@mozilla.com
description:
Sometimes we test natural enrollment for messaging experiments, in order to see what happens for e.g. first run users, or whether the user will enroll and the message will show before or after startup prompts. But it's hard to know what to expect when you don't know what branch you're enrolled in, which you'll currently need to use the console to determine. If about:studies showed the branch name then we could just open about:studies and see immediately if the experiment behaved as expected or not.

If we don't want to show the branch name to ordinary users, maybe we could lock the branch name display behind `default` release channel (unofficial), or behind the `nimbus.debug` pref for example.

Thank you!
summary: Show branch slug for experiments in about:studies

creator: nathanael.naeri@gmail.com
description:
Created attachment 9377371
Screenshot of the issue

User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Ubuntu; Linux x86_64; rv:122.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/122.0

Steps to reproduce:

I use Firefox with the menu bar enabled and the default System theme.


Actual results:

On Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, the menu bars of the windows are dark (as in a dark theme) even though the windows themselves are white (as in a light theme).

Firefox 121 respected those colors i.e. it displayed a dark menu bar and the rest of the window was white. Following update to version 122, Firefox displays a white menu bar (which incidentally makes it impossible to see the maximize/minimize buttons, but they're here).

Of course enabling the Dark theme in Firefox reverts to a dark menu bar, but then the whole window obeys the dark theme, not just the menu bar.

Note that this only concerns Firefox's main window: the "About Firefox" window and the bookmark manager window, for instance, have dark menu bars as expected.

Please see attached screenshot.


Expected results:

I expect Firefox 122 with System theme on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS to keep applying that OS's system theme: dark menu bars, white window backgrounds.
summary: Menu bar with System theme is wrong color in Firefox 122 on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS

creator: standard8@mozilla.com
description:
On `nsISearchEngine` we currently have three properties that all mention "identifier" in some form:

* `id` - the internal identifier of the search engine.
* `telemetryId` - the telemetry identifier of the search engine.
* `identifier` - if this is an application provided engine, this returns the `telemetryId`, otherwise it returns null.

This is confusing, as it really isn't clear what `identifier` is for.

Additionally, it isn't always obvious that identifier may return `null`, e.g. [this code](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/2c3d657cbba5484ccac44443c4417baed7b5fafb/browser/components/asrouter/modules/ASRouterTargeting.jsm#626) which returns an array containing `null`s if third party search engines are installed.

Another example is [filtering the `identifier` for falsy values](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/2c3d657cbba5484ccac44443c4417baed7b5fafb/browser/components/uitour/UITour.sys.mjs#1608) without mentioning why this is or might be necessary.

Therefore I think we should remove `identifier` and replace its use with `telemetryId`. If we need to filter out third party engines, then we can check the `isAppProvided` property of the engine.

The other alternative would be to replace `identifier` with a function, e.g. `getTelemetryId({ includeThirdParty: true})` so that it is explicit to include third party.

I'm not sure which method I like most at the moment.
summary: Remove nsISearchEngine.identifier

creator: chutten@mozilla.com
description:
bug 1877273 supports DOM's `dom.use.counters.dump.{document|page|worker}` prefs through generating individual cstring literals at codegen time via `usecounters.py`'s `metric_map` entrypoint. Pointers to these literals are returned from the `Increment(Worker)UseCounter(...)` functions (which is the only place where Firefox knows how to map from DOM use counter to Glean metric).

This bug is about investigating if there's a more pleasant way to do this. Logging is done infrequently, so maybe we can trade CPU for binary size? Or a little RAM? Or maybe just putting all the strings in a single place gets some gains? Maybe since the callers already know what the category is (doc, page, dedicated, service, or shared) we can omit the category and only print the name? Maybe we concatenate the category and the name at runtime only when needed?

There are options.

On the prior art front, Telemetry and FOG [both use `StringTable`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/toolkit/components/glean/build_scripts/glean_parser_ext/string_table.py) to store this kind of info (and, in fact, if `usecounters.py` knew [how to generate `metric_entry_t`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/toolkit/components/glean/build_scripts/glean_parser_ext/js.py#76) they could use the existing `StringTable` map of all metric identifiers that's accessible via `GleanJSMetricsLookup.h` (but that requires parsing all Glean metrics in the tree)), so that might be something to check out.
summary: Investigate more efficient use counter metric name string storage

creator: shughes@mozilla.com
description:
Currently, we only record reach [for 5 feature ids](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/6e2e933cd6b7931e1d4e8bd8af8daa9788b27760/browser/components/asrouter/modules/ASRouter.jsm#113-119):

```js
const REACH_EVENT_GROUPS = [
  "cfr",
  "moments-page",
  "infobar",
  "spotlight",
  "featureCallout",
];
```

But nowadays, there are many more messaging experiment feature ids that we'd want reach for. So, instead of using `REACH_EVENT_GROUPS` (which can be removed), we should use [`MESSAGING_EXPERIMENTS_DEFAULT_FEATURES`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/6e2e933cd6b7931e1d4e8bd8af8daa9788b27760/browser/components/asrouter/modules/MessagingExperimentConstants.sys.mjs). This will extend reach to the generic feature ids that we use when the named feature ids are already occupied.

The reason to do this is to reduce the risk of running an experiment where a precise exposure basis cannot be calculated. We need exposure or reach from the control branch to do this properly. But exposure is only recorded for control if the control message is a complete message (without content or template, to avoid actually showing something). If it's just an empty object `{}` exposure won't be recorded. And if that happens, reach is the only way to salvage the basis. But if the experiment is also on one of the `fxms-message-*` features, then we won't have that either, leaving DS with no option but to estimate exposure using past knowledge or some highbrow hackery beyond the comprehension of mere mortals.
summary: Record reach for all messaging experiment features

Fix transform of unary expression in Babel plugin


All of our static evaluation & dead-code elimination transforms need to
happen in post-order, transforming inner nodes first. This is so that
in complex nested cases all transforms see the simplified version of
their inner nodes.

For example:
  async getNimbusExperimentData() {
    if (!PDFJSDev.test("GECKOVIEW")) { return null; }
    // other code
  }
-> [evaluation of PDFJSDev.*]
  async getNimbusExperimentData() {
    if (!false) { return null; }
    // other code
  }
-> [!false -> true]
  async getNimbusExperimentData() {
    if (true) { return null; }
    // other code
  }
-> [if (true) -> replace with the if branch]
  async getNimbusExperimentData() {
    return null;
    // other code
  }
-> [early return -> remove dead code]
  async getNimbusExperimentData() {
    return null;
    // other code
  }

This was done correctly in all cases except for our `UnaryExpression`
transform, which was happening in pre-order.

description:
Created attachment 9377491
linkedin.html

We received reports about this behaviour on Instagram and LinkedIn where after closing overlay popups content on the page gets selected with a slight move of a mouse (bug1837615). I've attached a reduced test case. 

To reproduce:

1) Open the test case and click on the "Open Popup" button
2) Wait for the "pop up" and overlay to appear and click anywhere on the overlay
3) Move the mouse a bit and observe the behaviour

Expected:
Text doesn't get selected

Actual:
Text is selected

This only happens with a `pointerdown` event and not reproducible with a `click` event on the overlay. Both sites call focus() on the button element in the content before the popup is removed.  
Also I've noticed that not reproducible if I just hide the popup with `display:none`, it has to be removed from the DOM.
summary: Unexpected focus behaviour after pointerup event target is removed from the DOM

creator: continuation@gmail.com
description:
This is my second attempt at a spot fix for bug 1791283. My previous one, bug 1863852, dealt with the second test case but not the first one. In the second test case, the page with the stale alert is in the BFCache. In the first test case, I think the issue is that the window actually trying to create the alert is itself a current window global, it has a parent window that is not, so it is still not being displayed. My fix is to add a new function WindowGlobalParent::IsActiveInTab() that is like  WindowGlobalParent::IsCurrentGlobal(), but it also checks AncestorsAreCurrent to avoid this situation. It also checks the BFCache status on the top BC instead of the current BC, because Nika thought there might be issues with races (it is possible this is why my previous fix didn't work for the test case but I didn't investigate it). Hopefully this new function will do a better job at checking if a window is actually visible currently.

I wrote this based on talking with DOM: Navigation people. They said the name would more correctly be something like "isActiveInRootNavigable", but that's probably not a useful name to people writing Firefox JS code would might need this function. I did add a comment about that.

creator: t.broyer@ltgt.net
description:
Created attachment 9377691
firefox-progress-max-setting.html

Steps to reproduce:

Assign non-positive values to the max IDL property of a progress DOM element.


Actual results:

An equivalent string value was reflected to the DOM attribute, and on getting the max IDL property it now returns 1 (the default value for the max IDL attribute)

Tested in Firefox 122.0 (64 bits) and Firefox Developer Edition 123.0b5 (64-bit).


Expected results:

According to the rules for reflecting IDL attributes of type double that are limited to only positive numbers, setting a non-positive value to the IDL property should not change the DOM attribute's value, and therefore not change the IDL attribute value on getting: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes:idl-double

The progress element uses those rules for its max attribute: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-progress-element:reflect

Fwiw, WebKit (tested in WebKitGTK: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/17.0 Safari/605.1.15) follows the specification, Chrome however exhibits a similar problem, through slightly different wrt DOM attributes (https://crbug.com/1524023)
summary: Progress element's max property should ignore non-positive values on setting

creator: bmaris@mozilla.com
description:
**Found in**
* Latest Nightly 124.0a1

**Affected versions**
* Latest Nightly 124.0a1

**Tested platforms**
* Affected platforms: Windows 11, Ubuntu 22.04
* Unaffected platforms: MacOS 13 (even though something similar happens there as well, more details bellow).

**Preconditions**
* Have the Tab Hover feature active with `browser.tabs.cardPreview.enabled` as `true` in about:config

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open two websites in two different tabs.
2. Right click on the tab there is no focus on.
3. Hover over the same tab where the context menu is opened.

**Expected result**
* Hover effect is not active while context menu is opened.

**Actual result**
* Hover preview can still be used while having a context menu opened in the browser thus it is possible to have the hover overlap the context menu (Ubuntu) or the hover can be overlapped by the context menu (Windows).

**Regression range**
* Not a regression since this is reproducible on old Nightly build from 2024-01-13 where this feature officially landed.

**Additional notes**
* On Chrome and Firefox (Mac) the hover effect is disabled if having a context menu opened.
* In Firefox (mac included) the hover is also enabled if having hamburger menu opened, not in Chrome though. In Chrome the hover effect is active if Music control or Extensions menus are open but not their "hamburger" menu. We need to have a consistent behavior here I think.
* Probably this is not a specific Tabbed Browser issue but it does negatively affect this feature imho.
summary: Hover effect is active while having a context menu opened

creator: jteow@mozilla.com
description:
While smoke testing the SPA patch, there were a couple errors I didn't notice related to the content process:

1. In SearchSERPTelemetryChild, `addEventListenerToElements` doesn't just get called once per page load, so clobbering a possible existing `WeakMap` value will result in some listeners not being unloaded when manually tasked to do so.

2. If we register a click event in the content process that we want to take precedence over information sent in the network, namely clicking an auto-suggested term or submitting the search, [a check for an engagement will occur before the message from the child is sent](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/76cb3efe3b19e649bf675bb6ec5d4af8109b9771/browser/components/search/SearchSERPTelemetry.sys.mjs#613-625). 

We could first check if a submitted event was sent in the document, at which point we should not register an additional event.
summary: For tracked SPAs, accurately remove listeners from the content process and content specific engagements that cause search page changes

Screenshot showing the issue

**Found in**
* Latest Nightly 124.0a1

**Affected versions**
* Latest Nightly 124.0a1
* Firefox 123.0b4

**Tested platforms**
* Affected platforms: MacOS 13
* Unaffected platforms: Windows 11, Ubuntu 22.04

**Preconditions**
* Have `security.webauthn.enable_macos_passkeys` set to `true` in mac 13 or mac 14
* Have a iClould account connected to the used Mac.
* Have the Dark theme active in Firefox.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Visit https://webauthn.io/
2. Use a few usernames to register
3. Click the textarea where the username is entered.

**Expected result**
* All the passkey entries are easy visible in the autofill menu.

**Actual result**
* The icon of the passkeys is very hard to see when having the dark theme active..

**Regression range**
* Not a regression, this was introduced along with the Conditional Mediation feature enabled in bug 1865379 in Nightly 2024-01-17.

**Additional notes**
* The icons are clearly visible using the Light theme.
summary: Very hard to see icons of autofill passkey entries saved in iCloud with dark theme

creator: iireland@mozilla.com
description: jitsrc.py includes a variety of patterns for skipping past memcpy operations. Currently those patterns hardcode unnecessary information about which version of memcpy/memmove will be called: for example, the first rule matches against `__memmove_(avx|evex)_unaligned_erms`. The name of the memmove function depends on hardware support for various instructions. Instead of constantly adding new patterns for new hardware, we can simply match against eg `__memmove` and ignore the implementation details.
summary: Make jitsrc less picky about memcpy/memmove implementations

creator: nika@thelayzells.com
description:
In bug 1877672, the `FunctionRef` type is made to be `MOZ_TEMPORARY_CLASS` to prevent it from being used outside of a temporary context. This is being done to avoid issues with a temporary lambda being passed into the `FunctionRef`, which is then kept around longer than the constructor's expression.

Out of curiosity I noticed that absl has a similar `FunctionRef` type (https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/5c4a45eb17423373ecb71aea9819d41a6231613e/third_party/libwebrtc/third_party/abseil-cpp/absl/functional/function_ref.h#104), which has neither mitigation we have used for our type, but specifies this `ABSL_ATTRIBUTE_LIFETIME_BOUND` annotation. This appears to be a clang-specific annotation for cases like the one in bug 1877672 (https://clang.llvm.org/docs/AttributeReference.html#lifetimebound).

Unlike our custom static analysis, builtin clang attributes will be checked on developer's machines if they build with clang, without the clang-plugin enabled, meaning that it may catch bugs earlier in development.

This bug is to track potentially adding attributes for this annotation to `Attributes.h`, and potentially using it for our `FunctionRef` type (either in addition to `MOZ_TEMPORARY_CLASS` or instead of that attribute).
summary: Consider using `[[clang:lifetime_bound]]` attribute for FunctionRef

creator: iireland@mozilla.com
description:
The pseudo stack pointer on arm64 makes it easier to write platform-agnostic masm, but generates less efficient code overall. VM wrappers are hot enough that it's probably worth writing code a little more manually to trim the fat.

By my count, we can remove at least 5 out of ~40 instructions from each VM wrapper. Here's StringsEqual before, with the excess instructions marked with an X:

```
brk     #0x0                               // startTrampolineCode                         
sub     sp, x28, #0x8 (8)                  // make room for lr    
str     x30, [x28, #-8]!                   // push lr                                        
sub     sp, x28, #0x8 (8)               X  // make room for fp 
str     x29, [x28, #-8]!                   // push fp                                        
mov     x29, x28                           // move psp to fp                                 
mov     x0, #0x1700                        // load jscontext                                 
movk    x0, #0xc7e2, lsl #16               // ...                                              
movk    x0, #0x7fcc, lsl #32               // ...                                              
ldr     x1, [x0, #248]                     // load &cx->activation into x1           
str     x28, [x1, #112]                    // store psp into activation->packedExitFP        
mov     w16, #0x10d                        // load ExitFrameType::VMFunction (0xD) + vmID
sub     sp, x28, #0x8 (8)               X  // make room for it
str     x16, [x28, #-8]!                   // store it
sub     x28, x28, #0x8 (8)                 // make room for return value
mov     sp, x28                            // sync stack
and     x28, x28, #0xfffffffffffffff0      // align stack
mov     sp, x28                         X  // sync stack
sub     x3, x29, #0x10 (16)                // pass ABI arg
add     x2, x29, #0x20 (32)                // pass ABI arg
add     x1, x29, #0x18 (24)                // pass ABI arg
mov     sp, x28                         X  // sync stack
mov     sp, x28                            // do it again ???
mov     x16, #0xc808                       // load address
movk    x16, #0xc69f, lsl #16              // ...
movk    x16, #0x7fcc, lsl #32              // ...
blr     x16                                // call!
mov     x28, sp                            // sync stack
tst     w0, #0xff                          // check return value
b.eq    -> 1004f                           // fail on error
ldurb   w0, [x29, #-16]                    // load outparam into x0 via frame pointer
mov     x28, x29                           // restore fp to psp
mov     sp, x28                            // sync sp
ldr     x29, [x28], #8                     // restore saved fp to fp
ldr     x16, [x28], #32                    // load return address into x16
mov     sp, x28                         X  // sync sp
ret     x16                                // return to x16
```
And here is what we generate afterwards:
```
brk     #0x0                               // startTrampolineCode
sub     x1, sp, #0x20 (32)                 // allocate stack frame (sp < psp)
and     sp, x1, #0xfffffffffffffff0	   // align stack
str     x30, [x28, #-8]!		   // push lr
str     x29, [x28, #-8]!		   // push fp
mov     x29, x28			   // move psp to fp
mov     x0, #0x100			   // load jscontext
movk    x0, #0x2e2, lsl #16		   // ...
movk    x0, #0x7fc9, lsl #32		   // ...
ldr     x1, [x0, #248]			   // load &cx->activation into x1           
str     x29, [x1, #112]			   // store psp into activation->packedExitFP        
mov     w1, #0x10d			   // load ExitFrameType::VMFunction (0xD) + vmID
str     x1, [x28, #-8]!			   // push it
mov     x28, sp				   // sync psp (sp == psp)
sub     x3, x29, #0x10 (16)		   // pass ABI arg
add     x2, x29, #0x20 (32)		   // pass ABI arg
add     x1, x29, #0x18 (24)		   // pass ABI arg
mov     sp, x28				   // sync stack
mov     x16, #0xc628			   // load address
movk    x16, #0x2f, lsl #16		   // ...
movk    x16, #0x7fc9, lsl #32		   // ...
blr     x16				   // call!
mov     x28, sp				   // sync stack
tst     w0, #0xff			   // check return value
b.eq    -> 1004f			   // fail on error
ldurb   w0, [x29, #-16]			   // load outparam into x0 via frame pointer
mov     x28, x29			   // restore psp from frame pointer
mov     sp, x28				   // sync sp
ldr     x29, [x28], #8			   // restore saved fp to fp
ldr     x30, [x28], #32			   // load return address into lr
ret                                        // return to lr
```
summary: Generate better code for arm64 VM wrappers

Keith Cirkel <chromium@keithcirkel.co.uk> wrote:
>  Don't retarget nullptr in InvokeEvent::invoker
>  
>  This fixes a bug where dispatching an InvokeEvent with a null invoker
>  will cause a nullptr exception as it tries to retarget the Invoker based
>  on the currentTarget.
>  
>  The fix returns early nullptr if invoker is a nullptr, which also skips
>  the CHECK_EQ on eventPhase(), as just guarding the Retarget call would
>  skip to this check which would cause the check to fail if invoker was
>  retrieved during the bubbling phase.
>  
>  Bug: 1511341
>  Change-Id: I6e0e250a47466a502daeb8ab32335ff1521edc48
>  Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/5260418

>  Update IsElementReflectionAttribute
>

>  javascript getter will not be kept in sync. This patch adds the
>  popovertarget and anchor attributes to that list and also adds a DCHECK
>  to make sure that when the generated IDL code sets an element attribute,
>  that attribute is listed in IsElementReflectionAttribute.
>

Joey Arhar <jarhar@chromium.org> wrote:
>  Always call superclass in HTMLLabelElement::DefaultEventHandler
>  
>  HTMLLabelElement::DefaultEventHandler does not currently call up to
>  HTMLElement::DefaultEventHandler in many cases. This patch makes sure
>  that HTMLLabelElement always calls up to HTMLElement, which makes
>  \<label>s in \<button>s work.
>  
>  WebKit's HTMLLabelElement already does this in all branches of
>  HTMLLabelElement::defaultEventHandler since 2017:
>  https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/commit/fec9c1dd147617ff668b9ba8d7d1d4c31fac62de
>  https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/commit/b9bad3158f64ba11bca261380c244fbf4cfec31b
>

creator: jld@mozilla.com
description:
Found while testing a patch for bug 1875415: Valgrind also complains about memory leaks of various `strdup()`ed strings when the fork server is enabled.  These strings are part of argv/environ vectors at some point — we replace the original argv with heap-allocated strings copied from an IPC message, and we also relocate the original arg/env strings to the heap so we can overwrite the original arg/env space to implement `setproctitle`.  However, they become unreachable before the process exits — if they're dropped from the argv vector by a function like our `CheckArg` or dropped from the environment by libc's `setenv`.

There really isn't a way to free the strings when they become unreachable.  It would be possible to save copies of the pointers in an otherwise unused vector or something to make them “not leaked”, but it looks like we're willing to use valgrind suppressions in the case of setenv-like intentional leaks (bug 793548, bug 793549, bug 944133, and others).
summary: [forkserver] Valgrind reports memory leaks on strdup()ed env/arg strings

Sync web-platform-tests PR 44373 into mozilla-central (this bug is closed when the sync is complete).

PR: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/44373
Details from upstream follow.

Yi Xu <yiyix@google.com> wrote:
>  Revert "Remove empty closed paths"
>  
>  This reverts commit 572074cb06425797e7e110511db405134cf67e2f.
>  
>  Reason for revert: 
>  caused regression bug: crbug.com/1521614
>  
>  Original change's description:
>  > Remove empty closed paths
>  >
>  > As discussed in the github issue,
>  > https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1079, it's generally agreed to
>  > skip drawing line caps for closed paths. This is a follow up cl of:
>  > https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/4864061.
>  >
>  > In this cl, it verifies if each closed path is empty, then it removes
>  > the empty closed subpaths from path. As the subpaths are removed, the

creator: botond@mozilla.com
description:
I ran into this footgun while writing a new APZCBasicTester test: the APZC doesn't actually zoom in response to a pinch gesture unless you manually call `SetIsRootContent(true)`.

For single-APZC tests (using APZCBasicTester and its derived classes), the APZC should automatically have this flag set, to make the tests more reflective of production scenarios where there's almost always a root content APZC.
summary: Automatically set the is-root-content flag in single-APZC gtests

creator: botond@mozilla.com
description:
The [PinchWithTouchInput](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/14dc8f0e748d44778a02ffcf9ebcda3851b2bf9e/gfx/layers/apz/test/gtest/APZTestCommon.h#580) APZ gtest helper has a lot of optional parameters, making it cumbersome to use and especially to add new options to.

I'm going to clean this up by introducing a `PinchOptions` struct to store these parameters, which can be constructed with a fluent interface.
summary: Replace the optional parameters of PinchWithTouchInput with a PinchOptions struct

creator: botond@mozilla.com
description:
We have an APZ gtest called [TapFollowedByPinch](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/14dc8f0e748d44778a02ffcf9ebcda3851b2bf9e/gfx/layers/apz/test/gtest/TestGestureDetector.cpp#657) to test the scenario where a tap is followed by a pinch gesture, but the only thing it's testing is that the tap notification goes through (and that the APZC is not left in a dangling PanZoomState).

In this bug I'm going to expand this test to also check that the pinch successfully results in zooming.

(This came up during the review of bug 1798141; if the timing is right, the current version of the bug 1798141 patch can regress this scenario, and I want to add test coverage for this.)
summary: Expand test coverage of "tap followed by pinch" scenario in APZ gtests

creator: cbaica@mozilla.com
description:
Created attachment 9377908
amazon ES engine switch bug

**Found in**
* Fx124.0a1

**Affected versions**
* Fx 124.0a1

**Affected platforms**
* Windows
* Ubuntu
* macOS

**Preconditions**
Download an es-ES locale build.
Set browser.search.region to ES.


**Steps to reproduce**
1. Launch Firefox
2. Set Amazon.es as default search engine.
3. Go to about:config and switch to the new search config (set browser.search.newSearchConfig.enabled as true).
4. Restart the browser.

**Expected result**
* No info banner about the default engine is received.
* Default search engine is still Amazon.es

**Actual result**
* Info banner is received.
* Google is set as default search engine.

**Regression range**
* This is not a regression.

**Additional notes**
* Please note that when other regions are used, that also have amazon, like IT, US, GB (amazon.it, amazon.com, amazon.co.uk), amazon remains the default search engine after the config change and no info banner is received.
* Issue seems to only be with amazon.es, because it happens whenever that particular localization of amazon causes trouble. For example if I use the es-ES locale, have the region set to PT and have amazon set as default engine, the issue reproduces again.
* Later investigation uncovered that the issue is also happening for amazon.se as well. (locale: sv-SE, region: SE).
summary: Prior search settings are not kept when using amazon.es or amazon.se as default search engine

creator: nical.bugzilla@gmail.com
description:
The way things are currently set up has some performance advantages over simply remoting the pass encoing code to the gpu process but also bunch of disadvantages:
 - It forces wgpu-core's render pass code to use IDs instead of Arcs internally
 - It prevents us from moving registries out of wgpu-core
 - It made BGL dedup more complicated
 - It prevents some simplifications of the ID allocation/recycling code
   - That makes fixing https://github.com/gfx-rs/wgpu/pull/5141 more difficult
   - It also makes fixing out broken ID recycling more difficult
 - Forcing wgpu to have an internal `render_ffi` causes weird linking issues when people (accidentally) use two versions of wgpu.

For these reasons the wgpu maintainers would like to move away from this system which depends on Gecko remoting the render passes itself instead of serializing wgpu-core's internal representation.
summary: Don't run wgpu-core pass recording in the content process

creator: markh@mozilla.com
description:
Created attachment 9377938
image.png

iOS recently landed the ability to sync the "inactive" state of its tabs. This bug is for Desktop to not show these tabs by default, but instead add a new menu item, very much like the existing "Show more tabs" item, which shows these inactive items. See attachment.

To test this:
* You need a Firefox iOS 124+ - at time of writing, this means Nightly. Inactive tabs take quite some time to become inactive (2 weeks?), but you can force this by enabling the "secret menu" (open the settings menu, scroll down, then tab on the "Firefox XXX" version entry 5 times - new debug items should appear on the menu) then select "Set Inactive Tab Timeout")
* Wait a few seconds, and ensure that the "tab tray" in Firefox is showing some inactive tabs.
* Settings -> "Sync Now"

Then desktop will show something similar to the above.

Note that Android does not sync this yet, but I hope to get that working soon. If there are no inactive tabs then nothing changes.

This will change only the Synced Tabs menu. We expect Firefox View will probably want to do something similar.
summary: Synced tabs menu should hide remote "inactive" tabs by default

creator: dholbert@mozilla.com
description:
I was able to reproduce the intermittent failures in bug 1765787 locally a few times yesterday (though it stopped reproducing for me; it's very fiddly).

In the instances of the failure that I caught, it seems like the issue was this:
1. the test has a <browser> that starts out seeked to about:blank
2. the test immediately (in its load handler) calls  doPageNavigation to navigate that <browser>, and the test listens for a MozScrolledAreaChanged event as a signal that it can move on to the next part of the test.
3. BUT occasionally, in that first doPageNavigation call, the <browser>'s initial about:blank document **still has a pending reflow** which posts a MozScrolledAreaChanged when it completes (because its viewport size does change size -- maybe the outer test element resized or something as part of its load).
4. So the test's first doPageNavigation call occasionally receives that MozScrolledAreaChanged and misinterprets it as a sign that the first navigation completed, even though it's barely started.
5. ...and the test moves onto the next part of the test, despite that initial page not having been loaded in the <browser> and hence not being in the bfcache.
6. This results in us failing to navigate back (because there's nowhere to navigate back to) later on in the test, per bug 1765787 comment 38, and that explains this failure-mode:
```
TEST-UNEXPECTED-FAIL | layout/generic/test/test_bug514732-2.xhtml | Test timed out. 
```
...because the event that we're waiting for (from our back-navigation) never arrives, because we didn't actually navigate back.

Also: I think in some cases, our first doPageNavigation call **does** get a chance to complete and so we end up getting two MozScrolledAreaChanged events (the unexpected one from about:blank and the expected one from the actual page that we land on).  This explains the other failure-mode, which is:
```
layout/generic/test/test_bug514732-2.xhtml | Unexpected event (MozScrolledAreaChanged) occurred 
```

I've got a patch that I think will fix things by doing an initial load to a dummy page, where we simply watch for the `load` event instead of `MozScrolledAreaChanged`.  This should establish a more reliable initial state since I think the about:blank load event should not still be pending at that point and won't misfire in the same way that its `MozScrolledAreaChanged` event was.
summary: Attempt to prevent intermittent failure in test_bug514732-2.xhtml

creator: hello@lcas.dev
description:
Created attachment 9377986
Recording of the issue

An outer element has a key framed opacity animation with a fixed duration. An inner element has a infinite (looping) key framed transform animation.

In Firefox, the transform animation is very choppy while the opacity animation is running. This is not the case in WebKit and Chromium. Inverting the parent-child relationship of the animations (so the transform animation is on the outside, and the opacity animation on the inside) makes this bug disappear.

My hunch is that the outer opacity animation is throttled in some way, and this is incorrectly being propagated to the inner animation also.

creator: matthew@iammiller.com
description:
Created attachment 9378027
The section of WebAuthn L2 explaining when InvalidStateError should be raised

Steps to reproduce:

Complete the following steps on macOS 14.3 with a USB security key (I used a YubiKey 5 Nano) to reproduce:

1. Open Firefox's Web Developer Tools
2. Go to https://webauthn.io/?regUserVerification=discouraged&attestation=none&attachment=cross_platform&algES256=true&algRS256=true&discoverableCredential=discouraged&regHints=&authUserVerification=preferred
3. Enter a username
4. Click "Register" to call `navigator.credentials.create()`
5. Select "Security key" from the macOS system prompt
6. Complete registration with security key
7. Immediately click "Register" again
8. Check REGISTRATION OPTIONS in the browser console and confirm that the `"id"` of the credential returned from Step 6 is present in one of the entries in `excludeCredentials`
8. Select "Security key" from the macOS system prompt 
9. Complete registration with security key
10. Observe successful re-registration of the security key


Actual results:

Firefox allows the security key to be re-registered.


Expected results:

The `.create()` call should raise an `InvalidStateError` as per Step 20 in https://www.w3.org/TR/webauthn-2/#sctn-createCredential (see attached screenshot):

> If any authenticator returns an error status equivalent to "InvalidStateError",
> 
> 1. Remove authenticator from issuedRequests.
> 2. For each remaining authenticator in issuedRequests invoke the authenticatorCancel operation on authenticator and remove it from issuedRequests.
> 3. Return a DOMException whose name is "InvalidStateError" and terminate this algorithm.
> 
> Note: This error status is handled separately because the authenticator returns it only if excludeCredentialDescriptorList identifies a credential bound to the authenticator and the user has consented to the operation. Given this explicit consent, it is acceptable for this case to be distinguishable to the Relying Party.
summary: [WebAuthn] macOS Firefox 122 does not raise InvalidStateError on excludeCredentials collision

description:
`SyncedBookmarksMirror.sys.mjs` has [a helper called `anyAborted`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/34ba7989ae53b9112d543ce39d350b79dc2a16b4/toolkit/components/places/SyncedBookmarksMirror.sys.mjs#2574-2604) that takes two signals, and returns a new signal that aborts if either of the inputs abort. The bookmarks sync engine also uses a [`Watchdog` helper](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/34ba7989ae53b9112d543ce39d350b79dc2a16b4/services/common/async.sys.mjs#237-301) that [aborts merges that take longer than 5 minutes](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/34ba7989ae53b9112d543ce39d350b79dc2a16b4/services/sync/modules/engines/bookmarks.sys.mjs#494,500).

Bug 1830781 implemented `AbortSignal.any()`, and bug 1753309 implemented `AbortSignal.timeout()`, for these very use cases. Let's replace our hand-rolled helpers with them!
summary: Use `AbortSignal.any` and `AbortSignal.timeout` in bookmark sync

creator: g.maone@informaction.com
description:
Originally reported by a 김도훈_5791 to the Tor Project (tracked by [this issue](https://gitlab.torproject.org/tpo/applications/tor-browser/-/issues/42391)).

If a website uses IndexDB in a private browsing window, the storage files are encrypted with a key kept in RAM only, and put in a directory named `private`.
This directory gets removed as soon as the PB window is closed.
Unfortunately, if the  `browser.privatebrowsing.autostart` preference is `true` (Tor Browser's default) the `private` directory and its content are kept in place after browser's shutdown.

Steps to reproduce:

1. On a clean Firefox profile, set browser.privatebrowsing.autostart to true and restart the browser
2. Navigate to https://people.torproject.org/~ma1/test/idb/
3. Verify that a $PROFILE_DIR/storage/private has been created with encrypted db files inside
3. Quit Firefox

Expected result: the $PROFILE_DIR/storage/private directory doesn't exist anymore
Actual result: the $PROFILE_DIR/storage/private is still there with its content

Actually retrieving data from the encrypted database or even knowing which website it belongs requires searching a frozen snapshot of the RAM for the decryption keys, kept there during the browsing session. Furthermore you could always end in this situation if the browser just crashes, or if a determined and resourceful attacker manages to recover the encrypted files from the persistent storage after deletion.
Nonetheless I think we want this deletion policy to work as reliably as possible in global PBM as well, for consistency sake if nothing else.
summary: Private repository not removed on browser shutdown when PBM autostart is enabled

creator: ryanvm@gmail.com
description:
## Zydis v4.1.0
### Features
- Add `AVX-VNNI-INT16`, `SHA512`, `SM3`, `SM4` and `PBNDKB` ISA extensions by [@flobernd](https://github.com/flobernd) in [#449](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/449)
- Add `UD0_COMPAT` decoder mode by [@flobernd](https://github.com/flobernd) in [#477](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/477)
- Add support for loongarch by [@wuruilong01](https://github.com/wuruilong01) in [#462](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/462)
- Add `PCOMMIT` instruction by [@flobernd](https://github.com/flobernd) in [#429](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/429)
- Update instructions and add new ISA extensions by [@flobernd](https://github.com/flobernd) in [#407](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/407)
### Improvements
- Fix `ZydisFeature` enum max value constant by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#408](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/408)
- Excluded test tool from shared library builds (Fixes [#415](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/issues/415)) by [@mappzor](https://github.com/mappzor) in [#416](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/416)
- CMake: remove `CXX` from `project` directive by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#418](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/418)
- Use ZYAN\_DIV64 in ZydisStringAppendDecU64 by [@jpidancet](https://github.com/jpidancet) in [#424](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/424)
- Improve color output for `ZydisInfo` and `ZydisDisasm` by [@flobernd](https://github.com/flobernd) in [#433](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/433)
- Add missing static keywords. by [@jpidancet](https://github.com/jpidancet) in [#434](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/434)
- Convert ZydisDecoder field decoder\_mode to a bitmap. by [@jpidancet](https://github.com/jpidancet) in [#435](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/435)
- Add ZYDIS\_BUILD\_TESTS option and include tests in CMakeLists.txt by [@topazus](https://github.com/topazus) in [#437](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/437)
- Fix the installation location of manpages by [@topazus](https://github.com/topazus) in [#441](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/441)
- Build: fix amalgamation public header warning by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#440](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/440)
- Add missing `(void)` on functions without args by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#442](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/442)
- Fix ZYDIS\_FORMATTER\_PROP\_HEX\_FORCE\_LEADING\_NUMBER by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#452](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/452)
- Improve fuzzer stability in persistent mode by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#453](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/453)
- CMake: mark zycore dependency as required by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#457](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/457)
- Improve `ZydisRegisterGetLargestEnclosing` by [@flobernd](https://github.com/flobernd) in [#456](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/456)
- Check if Zydis is the top-level project for better FetchContent support by [@ZehMatt](https://github.com/ZehMatt) in [#459](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/459)
- CMake: improve search for Zycore by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#461](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/461)
- Fix [#463](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/issues/463): Wrong target offset calculated when using bnd prefix by [@ZehMatt](https://github.com/ZehMatt) in [#464](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/464)
- Fuzzing improvements and bugfixes by [@mappzor](https://github.com/mappzor) in [#466](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/466)
- Doc: extract documentation from all headers by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#467](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/467)
- Formatter improvements (sizes and addresses) by [@mappzor](https://github.com/mappzor) in [#472](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/472)
- Fix alignment issues with Intel macOS builds by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#475](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/475)
- Keep same order of files for amalgamation by [@evdenis](https://github.com/evdenis) in [#481](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/481)
- Reworked absolute address handling (Fixes [#471](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/issues/471)) by [@mappzor](https://github.com/mappzor) in [#473](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/473)
- Enforce predicted instruction size (Fixes [#478](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/issues/478)) by [@mappzor](https://github.com/mappzor) in [#479](https://github.com/zyantific/zydis/pull/479)
## Zycore v1.5.0
### What's Changed
- Better support for linux kernel by [@jpidancet](https://github.com/jpidancet) in [#62](https://github.com/zyantific/zycore-c/pull/62)
- Add `ZYAN_GETENV` macro to `LibC.h` by [@flobernd](https://github.com/flobernd) in [#63](https://github.com/zyantific/zycore-c/pull/63)
- Add missing `(void)` on functions without args by [@athre0z](https://github.com/athre0z) in [#64](https://github.com/zyantific/zycore-c/pull/64)
- Set DOXYGEN\_GENERATE\_MAN config option to generate manpages by [@topazus](https://github.com/topazus) in [#65](https://github.com/zyantific/zycore-c/pull/65)
- Add support for loongarch by [@wuruilong01](https://github.com/wuruilong01) in [#66](https://github.com/zyantific/zycore-c/pull/66)
- Support for more unix-like systems, such as NetBSD by [@niclasr](https://github.com/niclasr) in [#68](https://github.com/zyantific/zycore-c/pull/68)
summary: Update to Zydis v4.1.0 & Zycore v1.5.0

creator: drew.dani@outlook.com
description:
+++ This bug was initially created as a clone of Bug #1814722 +++

This broken again in Firefox 122 unfortunately.

Firefox 122 is accepting the FIDO2 PIN using the old webauthn popup mentioned [here](https://github.com/mozilla/authenticator-rs/issues/331), and then falling to send the request to the authenticator. Removing the AppID extension makes FIDO2 on-token PIN auth work with the new WebAuthn popup. I see a few major changes: to how the preflights in CTAP2 logic and a Rework support for AppId extension which appears to be where the bug was introduced.

The problem is when an AppId extension is provided for a FIDO2 security key, the user can enter the FIDO2 PIN, but then nothing happens after a user enters a PIN and clicks submit - the browser no longer talks to the authenticator. This is only a problem starting with the 122 release. It appears that starting Firefox 122, the default popup is the Apple/Safari one, however, when an AppId extension is provided, the old popup occurs and nothing happens after entering a PIN.

Code ref:
https://github.com/mozilla/authenticator-rs/commit/32f8e144eac287ec9ecb7b54c707e7c5bb32fbb0
https://github.com/mozilla/authenticator-rs/commit/d512ad9b5deb88edce20eca002659e469e4f8341

There are a couple of issues to report in the latest 

The [FIDO AppID extension](https://w3c.github.io/webauthn/#sctn-appid-extension) allows a relying party to request an assertion from a credential that was created using the legacy U2F javascript API. We seem to support this correctly in `U2FHIDTokenManager` but not in `CTAPHIDTokenManager`, i.e. not when `security.webauthn.ctap2` is true.

Users can work around this by re-registering their security keys.

This bug has been fixed in Firefox 114, but persists again in 115 and up. Can you please review the fix? The app id extension is no longer supported.
summary: The AppID extension is not responding to FIDO2/CTAP2 security keys in Firefox 122+

We should remove this code.

Ari Chivukula <arichiv@chromium.org> wrote:
>  [SAA] Implementing SharedWorker support (Part 3: Implement same-site cookie filtering)
>  
>  The Storage Access API provides access to unpartitioned cookies in
>  third-party contexts. This CL is part of a series to extend that access
>  to SharedWorkers.
>  
>  Before we actually provide access to SharedWorkers, we need a way for
>  the renderer to limit the scope of SameSite cookies provided to the
>  worker. Normally, a worker with a first-party storage key could access
>  all cookies, but if access is via the SAA handle we want to limit that
>  access to just SameSite: None cookies.
>  
>  This CL is part of a series to allow that limiting ability. It
>  implements the filter that prevents the inclusion of SameSite=Strict/Lax
>  cookies in a first-party shared worker when 'sameSiteCookies': 'none' is
>  set.
>  
>  Note: The ability to request 'all' in a third-party context is not added
>  here nor will it be added.
>  
>  Explainer:
>  https://privacycg.github.io/saa-non-cookie-storage/shared-workers.html
>  
>  Part 1: Expose same-site cookie IPC

creator: matthew@iammiller.com
description:
Created attachment 9378379
Firefox showing the user a choice when the RP communicates only a single valid option via transports in allowCredentials

Steps to reproduce:

Complete the following steps on macOS 14.3 with a USB security key (I used a YubiKey 5 Nano) to reproduce:

**Registration:**

(We have to use a different browser here until https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1878397 is fixed and we get transports from security key registration in Firefox)

1. Open Safari
2. Open Safari's JavaScript Console
3. Go to https://webauthn.io/?regUserVerification=discouraged&attestation=none&attachment=cross_platform&algES256=true&algRS256=true&discoverableCredential=discouraged&regHints=&authUserVerification=preferred
4. Enter a username
5. Click "Register" to call `navigator.credentials.create()`
6. Select "Security key" from the macOS system prompt
7. Tap security key (and enter PIN and re-tap if needed)
8. Observe in Safari's JavaScript Console that `response.transports` is populated with a USB transport (e.g. `["usb"]`)

**Authentication:**

1. Open Firefox
2. Open Firefox's Web Developer Tools
3. Go to https://webauthn.io/?regUserVerification=discouraged&attestation=none&attachment=cross_platform&algES256=true&algRS256=true&discoverableCredential=discouraged&regHints=&authUserVerification=preferred
4. Enter the same username as above
5. Click "Authenticate" to call `navigator.credentials.get()`
6. Observe in Firefox's Console that the `transports` property in the sole entry in `allowCredentials` contains `["usb"]` as seen during registration
7. Observe that Firefox prompts the user to choose between "iPhone, iPad, or Android device" or "Security key"


Actual results:

Firefox prompted me to choose between "iPhone, iPad, or Android device" or "Security key" via the macOS system prompt.


Expected results:

Firefox should have jumped straight to the security key option because the "iPhone, iPad, or Android device" option is for the `"hybrid"` transport which was not present anywhere in `allowCredentials`.
summary: [WebAuthn] macOS Firefox 122 does not respect transports during security key authentication
